verdict.rationale: The SFU is controlled through standard HTTPS APIs, and servers can take part in calls. Any WebSocket server, such as a Durable Object, can receive and send call media without implementing a WebRTC client, so headless server-side automation is a documented first-party mode. Nothing in the pack covers a CLI, CI integration, or a non-interactive test or automation workflow, so only the headless half of the story is evidenced. Missing for 10: CLI or CI tooling, documented CI/pipeline usage, hands-on corroboration of headless automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Use standard HTTPS APIs and WebRTC from browsers, embedded firmware, native applications, and servers.
Any server that accepts WebSockets, such as a Durable Object, can receive live call audio as PCM samples and video as JPEG frames without implementing a WebRTC client.
Use the Realtime SFU API to control which endpoints publish or receive audio, video, and data.
Your signaling backend can run on Workers, in a container, or on your existing infrastructure.
